title: Introduce KMS escrow assertion validator and audit hardening for private installs
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers running Redwood Private require stronger guarantees that customer-managed keys (CMKs) used during bootstrap are not accidentally re-scoped and that installer operations leave an immutable audit trail. This PR adds a KMS Escrow Assertion Validator to the private installer, hardens audit capture during bootstrap/migrations, and provides a non-disruptive migration path for existing installs. Motivation: recent customer reviews and an internal compliance audit highlighted two gaps: (1) the installer accepted KMS key ARNs/identifiers without validating provider assertions (origin, region, attributes), and (2) audit envelopes created during bootstrap could be mutated by post-install tooling. This PR addresses both issues to reduce blast radius and to meet SOC-like requirements for signed, append-only audit artifacts. Changes (high level): added a standalone validator component (installer/pkg/kms/validator.go) which verifies signed escrow assertions (provider fingerprint, region pin, tenant binding, timestamp, and nonce) against a configurable trust bundle; introduced an audit envelope signer and immutability flag (installer/pkg/audit/envelope.go) to ensure bootstrapping events are wrapped, signed (HSM/KMS), and stored append-only; extended the installer config schema and helm templates to accept trust bundles and audit retention policies; added a migration tool (installer/cmd/migrate-kms-assertions) that can scan existing installs and emit remediation suggestions without changing live resources by default. Checklist: - [x] assertion validator implementation + unit tests - [x] audit envelope signer + integration test harness - [x] helm values + docs updates - [x] migration tool + dry-run mode - [x] end-to-end smoke on GKE/AKS - [x] security review and threat model updated Commits summary: 1) initial validator scaffold and trust bundle parsing; 2) implement signature verification + region/tenant checks; 3) audit envelope signer + append-only writer; 4) helm/values + schema bump; 5) migration tool and dry-run; 6) tests, docs and bugfixes. Files changed (representative): installer/pkg/kms/validator.go, installer/pkg/kms/validator_test.go, installer/pkg/audit/envelope.go, installer/cmd/migrate-kms-assertions/main.go, charts/private-installer/values.yaml, charts/private-installer/templates/configmap.yaml, docs/private-installer/kms-escrow.md, scripts/e2e/smoke-kms-assertions.sh, scripts/ci/validation.yml, scripts/ci/integration-kms.yml, tools/trustbundle/generate.go, Makefile. Tests and CI: all CI pipelines passed on final run (unit, integration, e2e smoke). One flaky integration job (integration-kms) failed on first run due to ephemeral GKE quota; rerun passed. Security review: threat-model updated; recommended runtime KMS binding added to doc. Migration path and rollout notes: migration tool defaults to dry-run and emits remediation steps; operator must run with --apply to perform non-reversible changes. For installs that opt into enforcement mode (helm value kube.kms.enforceEscrow=true) the validator gates installer success and will fail fast on mismatch. Backwards compatibility: default install remains permissive (validator logs warnings) unless enforcement flag enabled. Rollout plan: soft rollout to internal staging by 2025-11-10, gradual enablement on customer canaries, disable enforcement by default for first two weeks while we gather telemetry. Rollback: helm can be used to disable enforcement flag; audit envelopes already written are append-only and preserved. Review conversation highlights: - Liam: "Overall looks good. Please add a test that simulates a wrong-provider assertion and ensure the migration tool reports it without applying changes." - Author: "Added validator_test.go with bad-assertion case and updated migration dry-run output to include remediation hints." - Sofia: "Need to ensure we surface a clear error message for ops when enforcement is enabled; current error string is too low-level." - Author: "Reworked error messages and added a grooming doc (docs/private-installer/kms-escrow.md#errors)." - Rohan: "Can we sign envelopes with either customer CMK or operator KMS?" - Author: "Yes — added selector logic and documented the trust model; default is operator-signed envelopes, customer CMK optional if provided and permitted by policy." Approvals and merge: after addressing comments the PR received approvals from all reviewers on 2025-11-18. CI green, security review completed; merged via squash on 2025-11-20. Release notes: "private-installer: add optional KMS assertion validator and signed, append-only audit envelopes for bootstrap; migration tool available in dry-run. Enforcement is opt-in via helm values (no behavior changes by default)." Impact and follow-ups: - Ops: recommend internal runbook update and canary enablement checklist in runbooks/ - SRE: add metric kms_validator.reject_count and audit.envelope.sign_latency to platform dashboards - Product: notify customers in security bulletin and provide migration guidance. Misc: no breaking API changes to installed services; installing with enforcement=true can fail boot if assertions are invalid (documented).
